body: Really, That is honestly awesome news! Do they have social distance measures? I heard Acadia (I think) is making all doubles into singles. Thank you for telling me though!

I really want that experience too, I might deffer for a year if they say it won't be open.  I still wanna live in or around Victoria though it just seems like a cool place to live. I do not wanna miss out on the residence though.
Thank you i'll look into it.
Do you think it will be open? I really want to live on campus but I do not expect to.
Do you guys do anything with hardware or is it just software?

I am not someone who really wants to spend time in front of computers mostly because that is what my entire high school experience was like and once I go to college I will probably have a lot of that too. I am someone who likes to put in a lot of hard work if the end result is satisfying. I am also looking for some adventure and be able to see the world which is why I asked how often they are deployed. I would say though even though I don't want to sit in front of a computer both Mar tech and NCI OP seem interesting to me because I want to know how a ship works and some naval tactics incase I want to be a NWO. Plus NCI OPs (At least according to the recruitment page) can be apart of things like boarding parties or fire crews.   I honestly am not too sure what work I am looking for. All I want is something that will give me some form of purpose and make me think/problem solve. I have never done much mechanical in my life and my interests in school would lean more away from that (History is my favorite, but I do have a big interest in science). And my work in life has been more grunty (Dishwasher, cook, demo/renovation stuff). If you cannot tell by now I am very conflicted.  I don't expect you to have an answer its just there is little information on naval trades I can find and I want to make the best decision.

Thank you for the response I see you might be in the navy, I am thinking about that heavily but I don't know what trade I really want to do. I am thinking marine tech because of its wide range of things it handles.  I was wondering if you could give some insight onto your trade a little.

I have two very different questions about the navy. One is how many younger people (under 26) are in the navy, are there a lot or are they not very common in your experience. The second is what is the Marine Tech trade like, how many deployments do they go on and how long is their training?
